newsitem.title: USA: Northwest Natural Gas seeks rate increase.
newsitem.headline: Northwest Natural Gas seeks rate increase.

text.p: Northwest Natural Gas Co said Monday it filed for rate increases averaging about 6 percent for its customers in Washington.
The utility said the rates in the filing are designed to increase revenues by $1.255 million a year.
The new rates would be effective July 1, 1997, if approved by the Washington Utilities & Transportation Commission.

Under the filing, rates would increase by 6.1 percent for residential customers, 5.9 percent for commercial customers, 5.0 percent for industrial firm customers and 6.1 percent for industrial interruptible customers.

Bruce DeBolt, Northwest's chief financial officer, explained that since the last general rate case, the number of the utility's Washington customers has quadrupled, and its investment in system utility plant has almost doubled.
The company said the rate filing is designed to recover its higher current cost of serving its customers.
